actors.name: Emeric

entries.look: A half-elf in road-stained leather with a lute on a frayed strap, mid-gesture, about to say something.
entries.bio: He was not born to the troupe, he was left with it. Half-elf children turn up in towns neither parent stayed long in, and a travelling company that needed a boy to hold horses did not ask questions. He learned lute, dice, three accents, and how to read a room before he learned to read.
entries.ties: The company broke apart when he was in his twenties — over money, or over a woman, depending on which version he is telling. He has worked alone since, which suits him considerably less than he lets on. He tells people he prefers the freedom. He is looking for them, and has never said so out loud.
entries.goal: To be the reason a room changes its mind. What he is actually good at is noticing; he will tell you it is the music, but the music is only the reason to be in the room.
entries.hooks: He remembers what people want and is usually glad to help them get it, which is generous and occasionally a problem — Halia will find that out before he does. Give him rooms rather than fights. Agatha at Conyberry is his scene: a performance for her earns a second answer outright. If the troupe ever turns up, do not announce it.

actors.note: Your own character. Point him at other people's moments, not his own.

actors.name: Amryn Velaris

entries.look: A high elf who stands where the light is worst, and looks like she is about to try something.
entries.bio: High elf wizard, chaotic neutral, one hundred and fifteen years old and barely an adult by elven reckoning. Old bloodline, one of the mountain strongholds, and every expectation that she would fall in line with the lawful orders. She wanted the primal stuff instead — fire and ice pulled straight from the source, no safety net.
entries.ties: She tried it. It levelled her family's laboratory and killed several conclave elders. Her standing was stripped, her family disowned her, and she was run out. She lives in the shadow of a mountain city that does not ask questions, and finds chaos suits her better than their rules ever did.
entries.goal: To reach the raw thing she was reaching for the first time, and survive it. And to find out who wrote the older hand — in the water-damaged spellbook, and on Don-Jon's map, in the same script.
entries.hooks: Fragile: threaten her with position, not damage. She is reckless and knows it, so give her chances to be reckless where the cost is visible in advance. The unrecognised handwriting is her thread — do not resolve it this campaign. Somebody from the conclave is still looking for her.

actors.note: 14 hp. Anything that threatens the paladin removes her in one turn. Ranged problems and cover, never a melee rush.

actors.name: Levi White

entries.look: A high elf in gold, and audible from a long way off. The greatsword is lit from inside.
entries.bio: High elf paladin, lawful good, and the fourteenth child of the royal house of Aurelion — a family in which only one heir is meant to survive to inherit. He was raised to fight his siblings and trained his whole life for the day he would have to kill them.
entries.ties: Outsiders invaded Aurelion and killed his father. Standing over the king's last breath beside his brother Callum, a beam of holy light came through the ceiling, took hold of Levi, and set him down in a country he had never seen.
entries.goal: To find out why the light chose him rather than any of the others, get home, and take back the throne. He has not decided what he owes his surviving siblings, and the question follows him.
entries.hooks: Level six against level twos. Never scale monsters up for him, that kills the rest — split objectives instead and give him the thing only he can hold. His whole life was a fight he was told he had to win alone; give him a choice where winning alone is the wrong answer. Do not hand him Icehewer.

actors.note: Level 6 against level 2s. Never scale monsters up to challenge him, that kills the others. Split objectives instead.

entries.look: A wood elf in furs with a two-headed axe across her back, checking the exits before the chairs.
entries.bio: Wood elf, soldier, chaotic good. Raised in a forest village where music and stories filled the trees, she followed her parents onto the road as a travelling entertainer, village to village, song to song.
entries.ties: War found the village. It was destroyed and her family vanished with it. She joined the army out of grief and anger, learned the axe she named Thornsong, and refused every order that would have harmed the innocent — which made her reckless in the reports and beloved in the ranks. She left when the war ended.
entries.goal: To make sure nobody else loses what she lost, and to keep hold of the entertainer she was before the war took a run at her.
entries.hooks: Give her the tracking, the weather and the terrain reads — she should be the one who notices the migration first and gets to be right about it. She was a performer before a soldier: put her in a room with Emeric and let them work it together. An order that would cost innocent people is the fastest way to find out who she is.

entries.look: A standing stone, split top to bottom, ice in the crack.
entries.detail: Elvish, older than the road. It marks a boundary with nothing on the other side of it any more.
entries.truth: Free reward for an all-elf party. Any of them reads it without a check: 'past here, we did not go.'

entries.look: A farm cart, tipped, half-buried.
entries.detail: The traces are cut, not broken. Somebody unhitched the horse and ran.
entries.truth: Nessa's cart. Put it where they will find it before they meet her.

entries.look: Iron bands, a good lock, and no dust on the lid.
entries.detail: The lock has been picked already, badly, and re-closed.
entries.truth: Whoever opened it first took one thing and left everything else, which is the interesting part.

entries.look: A basin of water that has not frozen, in a building with no roof.
entries.detail: The water shows the room you are standing in, one heartbeat late.
entries.truth: Savras. It answers one true question per party and the answer is never the useful one.

actors.name: Goblin

entries.look: Small, fast, and already moving to somewhere you are not looking.
entries.lore: Nature DC 10: they will not hold a line. They will leave and come back with friends.

narration: It shoots, then disappears behind the rock it was already standing near.

sections.label: Traits
rows: Takes the Disengage or Hide action as a bonus action on each of its turns.

sections.label: Actions
rows: Melee, +4 to hit, reach 5 ft. Hit: 5 (1d6 + 2) slashing.
Ranged, +4 to hit, range 80/320. Hit: 5 (1d6 + 2) piercing.

sections.label: Running it
rows: Shoot, hide, repeat. Never let one stand still and trade hits — that is the whole creature.
Six weak goblins in cover beat two strong ones in the open. Use cover, not hit points.

actors.name: Bugbear

entries.look: It was in the room before you were and you did not see it.
entries.lore: History DC 11: goblins obey them out of straightforward fear.

narration: The first you know of it is the reach.

sections.label: Traits
rows: A melee weapon deals one extra die of damage (included below).
If it surprises a creature and hits on the first turn, the attack deals an extra 7 (2d6).

sections.label: Actions
rows: Melee, +4 to hit, reach 5 ft. Hit: 11 (2d8 + 2) piercing.
Melee or ranged, +4 to hit, reach 5 ft. or range 30/120. Hit: 9 (2d6 + 2) piercing.

sections.label: Running it
rows: Worth 2d6 exactly once. Spend it on the opening round or not at all.
Stealth +6 on something with a morningstar. Open at reach, from cover, on whoever is furthest back.

actors.name: Twig blight

entries.look: A bundle of dead sticks, and then it is not.
entries.lore: Nature DC 12: they grow where something has poisoned the ground. Fire ends them fast.

narration: The undergrowth stands up.

meta: understands Common but does not speak

sections.label: Traits
rows: While motionless, indistinguishable from a dead shrub.

sections.label: Actions
rows: Melee, +3 to hit, reach 5 ft. Hit: 3 (1d4 + 1) piercing.

sections.label: Running it
rows: Run eight. They are a terrain problem, not a threat.
Vulnerable to it. Give the wizard the round she has been waiting for.

actors.name: Agatha

entries.look: An elf, or the shape of one, hanging a few inches above the leaf litter.
entries.rumour: They say there is a banshee in the wood east of Conyberry who answers one question.
entries.voice: Perfectly courteous, and about two centuries out of date.
entries.truth: She answers one question truthfully if offered a gift she considers beautiful. She has been dead long enough to be bored, not cruel.
entries.leverage: A comb, a mirror, a song. Emeric performing for her is worth more than treasure.

narration: She asks, politely, whether you have brought her anything.

meta: acid, fire, lightning, thunder; bludgeoning, piercing and slashing from nonmagical attacks
cold, necrotic, poison; charmed, exhaustion, frightened, grappled, paralysed, petrified, poisoned, prone, restrained

sections.label: Traits
rows: Senses living creatures within 5 miles and knows their kind.
Moves through creatures and objects as difficult terrain; 5 (1d10) force damage if it ends its turn inside an object.

sections.label: Actions
rows: Melee, +4 to hit, reach 5 ft. Hit: 12 (3d6 + 2) necrotic.
Each non-undead within 60 ft. that can see her: DC 13 Wisdom save or frightened for 1 minute.
Every creature within 30 ft. that can hear her and is not undead: DC 13 Constitution save or drop to 0 hit points.

sections.label: Running it
rows: This is a negotiation with a stat block attached. The Wail is there so the table understands the stakes of getting it wrong.
A gift she finds beautiful buys one true answer. Let Emeric try a song and reward it outright.

actors.name: Venomfang

entries.look: Green, coiled in a tower that used to have a roof, entirely unbothered by you.
entries.lore: Arcana DC 13: a young green dragon. Green ones talk. That is what makes them dangerous.

narration: It does not attack. It asks you a question, and waits, and appears genuinely interested in the answer.
It offers you a deal, and the deal is good, and that is the problem.
actors.note: Far above them. Venomfang is a conversation, not an encounter. If they fight, it kills someone and leaves.

stats.summary: Large dragon (chromatic), lawful evil — young green dragon
meta: blindsight 30 ft., darkvision 120 ft., passive Perception 17

sections.label: Actions
rows: One Bite and two Claw attacks.
Melee, +7 to hit, reach 10 ft. Hit: 15 (2d10 + 4) piercing plus 7 (2d6) poison.
Melee, +7 to hit, reach 5 ft. Hit: 11 (2d6 + 4) slashing.
30-foot cone. DC 14 Constitution save, 42 (12d6) poison, half on a success.

sections.label: Running it
rows: Always. It wants information and it wants to be flattered, in that order.
It is CR 8 against level 2s. Kill one character, then leave. Do not soften it, and do not let it become a grind.
It will trade safe passage for something it wants. Let that be a real option they can take.

items.name: Icehewer
items.text: A dwarven battleaxe with frost worked into the blade.
items.detail: +1 battleaxe. An extra 1d6 cold to anything not immune to it. The haft is wrapped in something that is not leather.
items.secret: From the Dragon Barrow. Do not hand it to Levi. Make the party decide who needs it, out loud.

items.name: A water-damaged spellbook
items.text: Three pages are still legible.
items.detail: Mage armour, feather fall, and a third page in a hand nobody at the table recognises.
items.secret: The unrecognised hand is Elvish and older than the book. It matches the second drawing on Don-Jon's map.

items.name: Gauntlets of ogre power
items.text: Leather and iron, much heavier than they look.
items.detail: Strength becomes 19 while worn. Attunement.
items.secret: Give these to Amryn's player rather than the obvious owner and watch what the table does with it.

items.name: Cloak of the winter hare
items.text: White fur, and it never seems to be wet.
items.detail: Advantage on Stealth in snow. Once per dawn, take the Dash action as a bonus action.
items.secret: Falcon made it and will not say from what. If asked directly he changes the subject exactly once.

items.name: Gnomish far-lens
items.text: Brass, articulated, and it clicks when you fold it.
items.detail: Doubles the range at which you can make a Perception check by sight. It also whistles, faintly, and cannot be stopped.
items.secret: Gnomengarde reward. The whistle matters if they try to hide from something with good hearing.

items.name: A coil of gnomish rope
items.text: Fifty feet, and it coils itself when dropped.
items.detail: It knots on command and unknots on a different command that nobody wrote down.
items.secret: The second command word is in Gnerkli's handwriting on a scrap in the store room. Let them find it later.

items.name: A plain silver ring
items.text: Sized for someone with narrow hands.
items.detail: Warm to the touch when worn. Advantage on saves against being frightened.
items.secret: From the Manse. It is elven and it was left behind on purpose, which is the interesting part.

items.name: A single white scale
items.text: The size of a dinner plate, cold to hold, and staying cold.
items.detail: It does not warm up. Left in a bowl of water overnight, the water freezes solid around it.
items.secret: Physical proof, so the argument in Phandalin stops being about whether and starts being about what to do.

items.name: An unsent letter
items.text: Found in the ranch house. Two lines in, the handwriting changes speed.
items.detail: Addressed to Neverwinter. 'Take them and go. I will follow when the cattle are down.'
items.secret: Narth wrote it and never sent it. Show it to him and he will not take it back.

items.name: Halia's ledger page
items.text: A single torn page of accounts.
items.detail: Three Phandalin names, three sums, and beside each a date that has not happened yet.
items.secret: Give this to one player and nobody else. The Zhentarim thread works best as one person's problem.

items.name: Nessa's charm
items.text: A bent nail on a bootlace. She gave it to you.
items.detail: She says her mother said it keeps the cold off. It does not.
items.secret: Worth nothing. Worth everything at tick eight. If a PC is wearing it when the dragon comes, say so.

items.name: Four sets of gnomish tools
items.text: Recovered, and none of them belong to anyone still alive.
items.detail: Each has a name scratched into the handle. Bexley. Torren. Wibbet. Anneth.
items.secret: Say the names aloud, one at a time. Do not summarise them.

items.name: A tally stick
items.text: Notched wood from the loggers' camp.
items.detail: Nineteen notches, then a gap, then four more in a different hand.
items.secret: Tibor kept counting after the crew left, so the numbers would look right.

items.name: A shed antler, cracked through
items.text: Found on the road north.
items.detail: It did not break on a tree. It broke from the inside, from freezing.
items.secret: Nature DC 13. A quiet way to make the cold feel like an agent rather than weather.

items.name: An orcish effigy
items.text: Bound sticks and hide, made in a hurry.
items.detail: It has wings, and someone has driven a nail through them.
items.secret: Yargath's people made it. They are not worshipping it. They are cursing it.

items.name: Axeholm's keyring
items.text: Four iron keys on a ring, all of them cold.
items.detail: Three fit doors you have seen. The fourth does not fit anything above ground.
items.secret: The fourth opens the cistern. Do not point at it.

items.name: A surveyor's map
items.text: Don-Jon's, covered in his handwriting.
items.detail: The excavation is drawn twice: once as dug, and once as it apparently should have been.
items.secret: The second drawing is older than the mine and not in his hand. It matches the Manse spellbook page.

items.name: Harbin's writ of commission
items.text: Official, stamped, and worth exactly as much as Phandalin's authority.
items.detail: It entitles the bearer to requisition from the town stores. Once.
items.secret: Cash this in during the evacuation. It is the only concrete thing Harbin ever gives them.

items.name: A deed to an empty house
items.text: Phandalin, one storey, needs a roof.
items.detail: Harbin hands it over instead of coin when the coin runs out.
items.secret: A base of operations, and a reason to care whether the town survives.

items.name: What the font said
items.text: Written down, because nobody trusted themselves to remember it.
items.detail: 'It will not be the cold that takes the town.'
items.secret: True, and useless, and correct in a way they will only see at tick seven.

items.name: Two potions of healing
items.text: Adabra's. She will not take payment.
items.detail: 2d4+2 each. She has more, and she will keep giving them away.
items.secret: Restock these whenever the party visits her. It makes the windmill worth defending.

items.name: A skin of Phandalin firewine
items.text: Toblen's, and stronger than it has any right to be.
items.detail: Advantage on the next save against cold within the hour. Also, disadvantage on everything else, briefly.
items.secret: Play the downside honestly and they will use it exactly once, at the right moment.

items.name: Three jars of gnomish pitch
items.text: Sealed, heavy, and warm through the glass.
items.detail: Thrown: 2d6 fire in a 5 ft square, and it keeps burning for a minute.
items.secret: The only ranged answer the party has to something that will not land. Make sure Gnomengarde offers it.

items.name: Cold-weather rations
items.text: Linene's, at a markup she will not apologise for.
items.detail: A week each. Without them, travel north of the lodge costs exhaustion.
items.secret: The one piece of resource pressure worth tracking. Do not track anything else.

items.name: A whistle that makes no sound
items.text: Bone, worn smooth, found in the barrow.
items.detail: Blowing it does nothing you can hear. Every dog and wolf within a mile turns to look at you.
items.secret: It works on the wolves at the lodge, and on nothing else. Let them discover the limit themselves.

items.name: A cup from the Manse table
items.text: Still where somebody set it down.
items.detail: Elven, unremarkable, and the water in it has not evaporated in three hundred years.
items.secret: If a PC drinks it, nothing happens, and they dream of the house as it was. Give that to one player privately.

items.name: A tarnished brooch
items.text: A hawk in flight, badly repaired at some point.
items.detail: Company of the Yellow Banner. Falcon's, or it was.
items.secret: He left it in the lodge deliberately. Returning it is worth more to him than gold.

items.name: A child's slate
items.text: From one of the northern farms.
items.detail: Somebody was practising letters. The last word is unfinished.
items.secret: Nessa's. Do not tell them that. Let her recognise it.

scenes.name: The Sword Coast North
scenes.description: Snow to the treeline, bare rock above it. Three roads meet in the low ground and Phandalin sits where they do.

entries.label: Opening the map
entries.text: The cold has stopped behaving like weather. It does not lift at noon. It sits on the valley with weight, and the smoke from Phandalin goes straight up because there is no wind left to move it.
One hex on the map is five miles. Phandalin to Icespire Peak is most of a day.
The old road north is faster, but it runs under open sky the whole way.
Livestock have been found split open and not eaten.
The woods have gone quiet in a way that is wrong for the season.

entries.label: A night on the road
entries.text: You get the fire lit on the third attempt. Above the treeline the sky is the clean, hard black you only get in a hard winter, and there are more stars than any of you have seen this far south. Some time before dawn, the person on watch notices that they have stopped hearing anything at all.

options: Travel to any pin they have heard of
Ask whoever tracks to read the season
Camp, and choose watches
Follow a track rather than a road
Push on through the night, and pay for it
Ask what an elf remembers about winters here

checks.success: Everything is moving south, and moving early. Nothing is moving north.
No predator does this. It is not feeding. It is marking.
Something passes overhead. No wingbeat: the sound is the air closing behind it.
This is not a season. Something is holding it here.

checks.when: On a frozen carcass by the road
checks.success: It froze standing up. Whatever happened, happened faster than falling over.

cues.text: Ask one player what their character does with their hands. Cold is a behaviour, not a number.
Nothing. Every time, until the once when there is something.
An elf reads it without a check. Let whoever speaks Elvish translate it aloud.

prep.threat: Exposure, and whatever is flying.
prep.wrong: The animals left weeks before the people noticed.
prep.notes: Travel is where the clock ticks. Never let a journey be free of information.

scenes.name: Phandalin
scenes.description: A mining town rebuilt on the bones of an older one. Mud, sled tracks, woodsmoke. Nobody here is older than the buildings and the buildings are not old.

entries.label: Arriving
entries.text: Conversation stops as you come up the road and starts again a beat later in a different key. Four elves is the most interesting thing to happen to Phandalin this month, and everybody has decided at once to pretend otherwise.
Townmaster Harbin Wester posts jobs on a board and does not leave the hall.
Refugees have started arriving from the northern farms.
There are more empty houses here than people to fill them, and nobody mentions it.

entries.label: Coming back, later
entries.text: There are more people in the square than there were, and fewer of them are working. Somebody has nailed boards over the north-facing windows of the Sleeping Giant, which is not a thing that helps, and everybody has looked at it and nobody has said anything.

options: Take work from the board
Drink at the Stonehill and listen
Sell to Linene, or try to
Ask Halia for something she should not give you
Talk to the refugees rather than about them
Talk to whoever is packing a cart
Ask Harbin what the plan is, and keep asking

checks.when: On Harbin, while he assigns work
checks.success: He is not sending you because you are capable. He is sending you because you are not from here.
checks.failure: He is nervous, but everyone is nervous.

checks.success: Nothing she has said is a lie, and nothing she has said is the reason she is talking to you.
checks.failure: She is a shopkeeper who is good at her job.

checks.success: She stops pricing you and says the drivers will not take the north road any more.
checks.failure: She quotes you a price and waits.

checks.success: Phandalin has been destroyed before. Twice. Both times everyone thought it would not happen again.

checks.when: Walking the square on a return visit
checks.success: Three more shutters boarded. Two more carts packed and not yet leaving.

checks.when: On Harbin, in front of anyone
checks.success: He folds completely and tells you the town has forty fighting adults and no plan.
Half of these were posted weeks ago and nobody has taken them.

cues.text: Quote everything ten percent high the first time. If they push back, drop it without comment. That is the whole prejudice, no speech.

cues.when: An old miner in the corner
cues.text: He saw elves once as a boy and has waited sixty years to tell someone. He is delighted. He is the counterweight.
Two people answer at once, differently, then look at each other.

cues.when: Once they stop explaining the cold away
cues.text: Reveal the Cryovain clock. Showing the track is itself a beat: they can suddenly see how much time is left, and the name at the top is the one nobody in town will say.

prep.want: Work, rumours, a bed that is not snow.
prep.threat: Nothing physical. Harbin will happily aim them at something lethal.
prep.wrong: Too many empty houses, and everyone has agreed not to see them.
prep.notes: The hub. Every return shows one thing worse than last time, tied to the clock rather than a schedule.

scenes.name: The Stonehill Inn
scenes.description: Two storeys, all of them warm, and the only genuinely comfortable chairs in fifty miles.

entries.label: Through the door
entries.text: The heat hits you like a hand. Somebody is playing something badly on a whistle, somebody else is telling a story they have told before, and for a moment the north is a rumour that happens to other people.
Toblen keeps the real job board. Harbin's is the one for show.

options: Perform, and see what the room gives back
Buy a round and ask about the north
Rent rooms and take a long rest
Read the unofficial board

checks.success: The room turns. Advantage on the next social check anyone in the party makes tonight.

checks.when: Watching the room rather than the fire
checks.success: Nobody sits with their back to the north window. Not one person.
checks.failure: A warm room full of tired people.

cues.text: Give the bard the room, then let another player choose what the crowd does with it.
Somebody says 'dragon' as a joke, and the room goes quiet for exactly one second too long.

prep.want: Rest, and the version of the news people only tell indoors.
prep.threat: None. Protect this place, the campaign needs one room that is safe.
prep.wrong: The refugees are sleeping in the stable and Toblen has quietly stopped charging them.

scenes.name: Gnomengarde
scenes.description: A rock-gnome warren pressed into a granite hillside. Every door is slightly too short. The air smells of hot brass and burnt sugar.

entries.label: At the door
entries.text: Somewhere behind the walls a mechanism is running that nobody has turned off in years. You feel it in the floor before you hear it. A gnome opens a hatch at knee height, looks at your boots, says 'yes, good, excellent,' and closes it again.
Two kings rule here, Dabbledob and Gnerkli, and both of them want out.
Gnomes have gone missing. The kings will not say how many.
The lower stores are sealed, and the kings sealed them.

entries.label: When it turns
entries.text: Gnerkli has stopped talking. He is looking at the barred door and he is not looking at you, and when he finally speaks it is not an answer to anything you asked. He says: 'It was already in there. I only stopped it getting out.'

options: Accept the crown, and see how far Dabbledob takes it
Separate Gnerkli from Dabbledob
Count the beds, the bowls, the coats on hooks
Trade for an invention nobody will guarantee
Open the barred door
Ask for pitch, rope, or a lens as payment
Ask what the mechanism was for

checks.success: Beds, bowls, coats. The number is wrong by four, and nobody corrects it.
checks.failure: Gnomes, and a great deal of clutter.

checks.success: He is not evading you. He is waiting to be asked a direct question by somebody kind.
checks.failure: He looks at the door again.

checks.when: On the storage chest in the lower hall
checks.success: The grain of the wood does not run the right way.
Barred from this side. Recently. By someone short.

checks.when: Standing still in the lower hall
checks.success: Under the mechanism there is another sound, and it has a rhythm, and the rhythm is chewing.
checks.failure: The machine, and only the machine.

checks.success: Dabbledob produces paperwork. Actual paperwork. He has had it ready for months.
checks.failure: He laughs, and does not stop.

checks.success: Nobody sees. Later, everybody knows, and nobody mentions it.
checks.failure: A gnome sees, and says nothing, loudly.

checks.success: Cut, not broken. Recently. By somebody who could reach it standing up.

cues.text: Cheerfully, completely, and about something else. Nobody lies. Everyone deflects.
It is barred from this side. Let a player say that out loud.
Do not have the kings apologise. Have Dabbledob offer the crown again, immediately, as though nothing happened.

prep.want: The kings' reward, and whatever the workshops are worth.
prep.threat: The thing in the sealed store, and a warren of gnomes who will not warn them.
prep.wrong: Every gnome answers cheerfully and none of them answers the question.
prep.notes: The turn is not the monster. It is when they realise the disappearances were never a mystery to the kings.

scenes.name: Umbrage Hill
scenes.description: A windmill on a bare hill, and a great deal of blood in the snow that will not wash out until spring.

entries.label: After the fight
entries.text: It is over, and the hill is very quiet. Adabra Gwynn comes out with a bucket, looks at the thing in the snow, looks at you, and says: 'It came down the hill. Nothing comes down that hill.'
Adabra Gwynn lives here alone and midwifes for the whole region.
The manticore was driven down from higher ground by something larger.

options: Examine the body
Convince Adabra to come to town
Ask what she has been treating lately
Look uphill, at where it came from
Ask about the last person she treated for cold

checks.success: No wounds on its back. It was not running from a fight. It was just running.
checks.failure: It is very dead and very large.

checks.success: One set of tracks down. Nothing following. Whatever moved it did not need to chase it.
checks.failure: The snow has filled everything in.

checks.success: She refuses, and tells you why: her mother is under the floor.
checks.failure: She refuses, and does not explain.

checks.success: Something struck it once, from above, and did not follow it down.
She is not frightened. She is furious, and she is furious about something older than today.

cues.text: No wounds on its back. It was just running.
Refuses. Do not soften it.

prep.want: Already taken. Adabra owes them now.
prep.threat: Cleared.
prep.wrong: The manticore came here to get away from something.

scenes.name: The Dwarven Excavation
scenes.description: A hillside opened like a wound, three dwarves living in it, and a great deal of very old stonework behind them.

entries.label: Over the ridge
entries.text: There is a hole in the hill somebody made on purpose, and shoring timbers going into it much newer than the stone they hold up. A dwarf stands on a crate arguing with two others about whether the crate is load-bearing.
What they have broken into is older than the mine, and older than the dwarves who built the mine.

entries.label: The lower gallery
entries.text: The lantern reaches the far wall and the wall is not dwarven. The stone is dressed differently, jointed differently, and it has been standing here in the dark long enough that the dwarves' own two-hundred-year-old work looks like scaffolding against it.

options: Take Don-Jon's contract
Go down
Ask what they were actually digging for
Read the carvings
Ask to see the original assay

checks.when: On the carvings below the dwarven layer
checks.success: The work changes hands halfway down. Elvish beneath, dwarvish above, and the elvish is far older.
He is not surprised by what is down there. He is surprised you noticed.

checks.when: On the jelly, before it reaches anyone
checks.success: Slashing splits it. Do not.
checks.failure: It is yellow and it is moving.

checks.success: New wood on old stone, and the old stone does not need it.
They confirm what Don-Jon will not: there was no ore in the assay.

cues.text: The jelly comes through a gap nobody was watching. Split it the first time somebody uses a blade.
The carving changes hands. Your all-elf party will notice, and should get to feel clever about it.

prep.want: Dwarven pay, and what is under the dwarven pay.
prep.threat: An ochre jelly in a corridor with one exit.
prep.wrong: Don-Jon has stopped pretending they are digging for ore.
prep.notes: Give the elves the older layer. It costs nothing and makes their race a fact about the world.

scenes.name: Falcon's Hunting Lodge
scenes.description: A well-built lodge where a well-built lodge has no business being, with a man outside it listening to the treeline rather than to you.

entries.label: Falcon, when it lands
entries.text: He does not look surprised. That is the thing you notice. Everyone else in this valley has been surprised for a month, and this man has not been, and has not been for some time.
Falcon served with the Company of the Yellow Banner, a long way south of here.

entries.label: If they stay the night
entries.text: He does not sleep. Some time after midnight you find him on the porch with a bow across his knees, looking north at nothing in particular, and he says, without turning round: 'It goes over about now. Most nights.'

options: Hire him as a guide
Ask what he did before the lodge
Say the word 'dragon' and watch him
Deal with the wolves for him
Stay the night and see what he does

checks.success: He has been waiting for somebody to ask the right question, and getting quietly angrier that nobody has.
A mercenary company that broke up after something in the south nobody names.
checks.failure: The name means nothing to you.

checks.success: They are starving, not hunting. Food ends this without a fight.
checks.failure: They are wolves and they are close.

checks.success: Every sightline is cleared. Deliberately. Recently.
A brooch on the mantel, tarnished, a hawk in flight.

cues.text: He stops moving. That is the reveal. No speech.
He will not, until the clock reaches six. Then he arrives without being asked.

prep.want: A guide, and somebody who is not frightened.
prep.threat: Wolves ranging far further south than they should.
prep.wrong: He knew before anyone. He has been waiting to be asked.

scenes.name: Butterskull Ranch
scenes.description: A ranch house with the roof partly off, cattle scattered across four fields, and no people at all in the first minute you are here.

entries.label: The yard
entries.text: The front door is inside the house. Something put it there. In the yard a cow stands perfectly still beside a trough frozen solid with the ladle still in it.
Orcs came through, and they were not hunting. They were moving.
One of the orcs is wounded in a way nothing at this ranch could have done. Cold, not a blade.

entries.label: When it is over
entries.text: Narth Tezrin comes up the track an hour later with a shovel over his shoulder and stops when he sees the yard. He looks at the orcs, and at the door that is inside his house, and at you, and the first thing he says is: 'Are the cattle all right.'

options: Fight the orcs
Talk to them first, Yargath will answer
Search the house
Round up the cattle, which matters more than it sounds
Ask Yargath where his people came from
Help Narth put the door back

checks.when: On the wounded orc, alive or dead
checks.success: Frostbite that went to the bone in seconds. Nothing on this ranch does that.
A letter, two lines in, where the handwriting changes speed.

checks.when: Opening with words instead of steel
checks.success: Yargath will talk. He will tell you exactly what came down the mountain, and that his people are running from it too.
checks.failure: He watches to see whether you will attack, and then obliges.

checks.success: They can be brought in. Narth will notice that you did.

checks.when: On Yargath, before anything is decided
checks.success: He has been ready for a fight and would rather not have one.
checks.failure: He is an orc with an axe.

checks.when: On the orcish effigy in their camp
checks.success: Bound sticks with wings, and a nail driven through them.
He is asking about the cattle because he cannot yet ask about anything else.

cues.text: Aggressive: the orcs run past the armour to reach the wizard. Narrate it as it happens, so the party learns the rule by watching.
Fine. Yargath's information arrives later through Falcon instead. Never gate the plot behind one conversation.

prep.threat: Orcs who close immediately and always.
prep.wrong: The orcs are refugees too.
prep.notes: The cold wound is the clue. Do not point at it.

scenes.name: The Loggers' Camp
scenes.description: Cut timber stacked in rows, a cookfire that has been out for two days, and one man insisting everything is fine.

entries.label: Walking in
entries.text: Someone has stacked the timber beautifully. Someone else has stopped. There is a line across the camp where the work simply ended, and everything on the far side of it is exactly where it was dropped.
Half the crew walked out a week ago, and Tibor did not report it.

options: Get the truth out of Tibor
Deal with the ankheg
Follow the crew's tracks south
Finish the count of who is missing
Offer to bring the crew back
Ask who the tally is for

checks.success: He admits the crew left. He admits he did not tell his cousin. He asks you not to.

checks.when: On the churned ground between the stacks
checks.success: It hunts by vibration. Standing still works. Running does not.
They went south, together, fast, and none of them looked back.

checks.when: On the cookfire and the bedrolls
checks.success: Nineteen bedrolls. Four of them have been slept in this week.
He is not hiding a crime. He is hiding that he has been alone here for a week.

cues.text: Never appear where they are looking. Come up under whoever moved last round.
He is grateful in the most embarrassing way possible, loudly, in front of Harbin, later.

prep.want: Payment, and to know where the crew went.
prep.threat: An ankheg under an open camp with no cover.
prep.wrong: Tibor has been alone here for a week pretending he is not.

scenes.name: Axeholm
scenes.description: A dwarven fortress dug into a hillside, abandoned for two hundred years, with the doors still closed and still holding.

entries.label: The gate
entries.text: The doors are shut and undamaged, which is the wrong thing for a ruin. Whatever emptied this place did not come in through the front.
There is water under the fortress, and something in the water.

entries.label: The great hall
entries.text: Two hundred years of nothing. No bodies, no scorching, no broken furniture. Somebody swept this floor before they left it, and then barred the door behind them, and then went somewhere you cannot see from here.

options: Find a way in that is not the gate
Use the keyring if they have it
Bring the refugees here, if the clock is high
Go down to the cistern
Count how many it could hold
Repair the gates, given timber

checks.success: Barred from inside. Whoever left, left another way, and left it barred behind them.

checks.when: On the armour in the hall
checks.success: Bound, not undead. It is guarding a line on the floor, not the room.

checks.when: In the cistern, at the cold
checks.success: Not a ghost. Something the cold made once the cold got old enough. It will not follow you into daylight.
checks.failure: It is very cold and you would like to leave.

checks.success: A keyring, four keys, all of them cold.
They evacuated. In order. Two hundred years ago, and for a reason nobody wrote down.
The fourth key fits. Of course it does.
checks.failure: A hatch, and no way through it.

checks.when: On the fortress as a refuge
checks.success: Two hundred people could hold this with forty defenders, if the gates were repaired.
checks.failure: It is big and it is cold.

cues.text: Show them the line on the floor before the fight, not after.
Fight it at night or not at all. If they work out the sunlight clause, give it to them immediately.

cues.when: If the clock is at six or higher
cues.text: This is the evacuation site. Let a player propose it. If nobody does, have Falcon propose it.

prep.threat: A shade that ignores your lantern.
prep.wrong: The doors are barred from the inside and nobody is in here.
prep.notes: This becomes the evacuation site at clock six. Plant it early so it is theirs, not yours.

scenes.name: The Woodland Manse
scenes.description: An elven house in the woods, roofless, with the forest growing through it politely rather than destroying it.

entries.label: Inside the wall
entries.text: The trees have not broken this house. They have grown around it, carefully, the way you step around someone sleeping. The floor is still level. Somebody's cup is still on the table.
This is elven work, and older than any elf currently alive.

entries.label: The table
entries.text: There is a cup on the table with water still in it. Not rain. Not meltwater. It has been sitting in an open room for longer than any of you have been alive and it has not evaporated, and it has not frozen, and nobody has moved it.

options: Read the house, which any elf can do without a check
Find the spellbook
Ask who lived here, and get an answer nobody likes
Take nothing, which is also a choice
Sit down at the table, which is a thing you can do
Leave the cup where it is

checks.success: Not abandoned. Left. Deliberately, in order, with the cups put out.
A spellbook, three legible pages, and a fourth in a hand nobody recognises.
Every window faces north. All of them. There are no south windows at all.
The water is held, not preserved. Somebody meant to come back and finish drinking it.
A plain silver ring, left on a sill, deliberately.
The wood is completely silent. No birds. Not because something scared them off — because they were never here.

cues.text: No check. They know what this is, and that it was left rather than lost.
It is older than the book. Do not explain it this session, or the next.

prep.want: The spellbook, and a piece of their own history.
prep.threat: Spiders in a house with no roof and no cover.
prep.wrong: Everything is where it was put down. Nothing was taken.
prep.notes: This is the elf party's scene. Give it to them and stay out of the way.

scenes.name: The Dragon Barrow
scenes.description: A grave-mound on open ground, opened once already, with the stone rolled aside and never rolled back.

entries.label: At the mouth
entries.text: Somebody buried something here under a great deal of earth and a great deal of intention. Somebody else has since decided that was a mistake, and has left the door open behind them.
A dragon was killed here once, and the people who killed it were buried with it.

options: Go in
Read the stone
Leave it, and say why
Put the stone back afterwards, which somebody will suggest

checks.success: Not a dragon's grave. The grave of the people who killed one, buried with what it cost them.
Paralysis. Elves are immune. Tell the elf who asked, out loud, at the table.
checks.failure: They are dead and they are moving.

checks.success: Icehewer, and the hand that was holding it.
The stone was moved from outside, and recently, and by more than one person.

checks.when: On the bodies in the antechamber
checks.success: Not looted. Arranged. Somebody laid them out after they died.

cues.text: An all-elf party walks through this. Let them. A fight they trivialise because of who they are is a reward, not a waste.
Do not hand it to the paladin. Make the party choose who needs it.

prep.threat: Ghouls in a corridor, against a party immune to their best trick.
prep.wrong: The stone was rolled aside from the outside, recently.

scenes.name: The Shrine of Savras
scenes.description: A roofless shrine to a god of prophecy, with one man still living in it and a basin of water that has not frozen.

entries.label: The Anchorite
entries.text: He is answering a question before you have asked it, and it takes a moment to work out that the answer is correct. Behind him a basin of open water sits in a building with no roof, in weather that has frozen a well inside a walled town.
The font answers one true question per party, and the answer is never the useful one.

options: Ask the font a question, once
Ask the Anchorite instead, which is worse and better
Bring him to Phandalin
Leave him where he is
Write the answer down before you interpret it

checks.success: One question, one true answer, and no promise that the answer helps.
Everything he says is true. None of it is useful yet. Both are on purpose and neither is his fault.
He has not eaten in days and has not noticed.
checks.failure: He seems fine, in his way.

checks.when: Asking the Anchorite to come to Phandalin
checks.success: He agrees immediately and asks whether he should bring the font.
checks.failure: He is already answering a different question.

checks.when: On why the water has not frozen
checks.success: It is not warm. It is simply not participating.

cues.text: Answer honestly and unhelpfully. Write the answer down before they ask if you can, so it feels fixed.
He answers the question they are about to ask. Do this exactly twice, then stop.

prep.threat: None here. The threat is what they do with the answer.
prep.wrong: The water has not frozen, and everything else for forty miles has.

scenes.name: The Tower of Storms
scenes.description: A broken tower on a headland over the sea, with the surf coming up through the floor of the lowest room.

entries.label: On the headland
entries.text: The wind here is doing something wind should not: going round the tower rather than over it. The stone is warm. Everything else on this coast is not.
Something old is being worshipped here, and it has drawn things up out of the water.

options: Fight on the rocks, which is a bad idea and available
Fight inside, which is worse
Cut the harpoon lines
Break whatever is keeping the stone warm
Fight it on a timer, with the tide coming in

checks.when: On the rocks before anything happens
checks.success: The surf has a rhythm and something in it does not.
Sea ogres. They do not come this far north unless something moved them.

checks.when: Cutting a harpoon line before it pulls
checks.success: You cut it. Whoever it had goes down on the rock instead of into the water.
checks.failure: The line holds and somebody goes over.

checks.success: Something under the tower is being fed, and it has been fed recently.
Two hours until the lower room floods. Set a clock and mean it.

cues.text: The fight is the edge, not the damage. Make the drop matter.
Cold water this far north is a countdown, not a swim check.

prep.want: To stop whatever is calling things out of the sea.
prep.threat: Merrow with harpoons on a ledge above cold water.
prep.wrong: The stone is warm.

scenes.name: Icespire Hold
scenes.description: A ruined fortress on the shoulder of the peak, wind coming through it in three directions, and something living on the top floor.

entries.label: The approach
entries.text: There is no snow on the stone. That is the first thing that is wrong. Everything for a mile is white and the hold is bare grey rock, because everything that lands on it has been melted and frozen and melted again by something breathing.
This is where it sleeps.
There are older bones here than the cattle it has been taking.

entries.label: The top floor
entries.text: It is awake. It has been awake the whole time you were climbing, and it has let you climb, and now it turns its head about two inches to bring one eye to bear on the four of you and it does not get up.

options: Go up
Set something on the roof and wait
Bring Falcon
Leave, one last time
Take the long way and arrive unseen
Send one person in through the roof

checks.success: There is one route up that is not visible from the air. It takes an hour longer.
checks.failure: One way up, in the open.

checks.success: Bones under the bones. It did not make this lair. It took it.
It has been here longer than a month. Far longer.

checks.when: On the dragon, before anything is thrown
checks.success: It is not going to negotiate, but it is curious, and curiosity is time.

checks.when: On the roof, before going in
checks.success: There is a hole in the roof it uses. It is big enough for you, and it does not expect that.
You arrive out of sight and out of breath, with surprise.

cues.text: Give them one clean chance to leave, and mean it. A last exit they refuse is worth more than one you never offered.
Ask each player what their character does with the fear before anybody rolls. Then roll.
It does not finish them. It moves to the next one. That is characterisation, not mercy.

prep.threat: A young white dragon on ground it chose.
prep.wrong: There are older bones here than anything it has killed.
prep.notes: Not before level 5, and not before clock seven. If they come early it is out hunting, and they can see what it sleeps on.

scenes.name: Axeholm, lower level
scenes.description: Below the great hall: storerooms, the barracks, and the cistern the fourth key opens.

entries.label: Down the stair
entries.text: The stair turns twice and the air changes on the second turn. It is not colder, exactly. It is stiller, the way a held breath is still.
The storerooms were emptied properly. Shelves swept, nothing spoiled, nothing left.

options: Open the cistern
Search the barracks
Go back up while you still want to

checks.success: Two hundred bunks, and every one stripped. They packed.
The cold in there is not weather and it is not a ghost.

cues.text: Fight it at night or not at all. If they find the sunlight clause, give it to them at once.

prep.threat: A shade in a flooded room with one way out.
prep.wrong: Everything was packed. Nobody panicked. So what made two hundred dwarves leave in order?

scenes.name: Umbrage Hill, milling floor
scenes.description: Inside the windmill: the millstone, the grain chute, and Adabra's whole surgery on one table.

entries.label: Through the door
entries.text: Herbs on strings, a scrubbed table, and a row of instruments laid out in the order she uses them. This is a working room, and the work is keeping people alive.
She has far more healing potions than one windmill should hold, and gives them away.

options: Ask her to teach somebody first aid
Look at what she is short of
Go up

checks.success: She is out of three things she cannot get since the road closed.
A second set of instruments, sized for a child's hands, never used.

cues.text: She accepts immediately and puts them to work. She does not thank people, she uses them.

prep.threat: None. Keep it that way.
prep.wrong: The unused child-sized instruments, which she will not explain.

scenes.name: Umbrage Hill, the cap
scenes.description: The top of the windmill, level with the sails, and the best view north for twenty miles.

entries.label: At the top
entries.text: You can see the whole valley from here, and the peak above it, and the exact line where the snow stops being seasonal and starts being something else.
From the cap you can see Icespire Peak, and something circling it.

options: Watch the peak
Post a lookout here
Signal Phandalin

checks.success: Something is circling it, unhurried, and it has been circling for as long as you have watched.
Every track in the snow runs south. You can see it as a pattern from up here.

cues.text: Do not name it. Let them describe what they see and correct nothing.

prep.threat: A long fall, and being seen from the air.
prep.wrong: It is circling. It has been circling the whole time.

scenes.name: The Woodland Manse, upper floor
scenes.description: Bedrooms open to the sky, a gallery with every window facing north, and dust that has never been disturbed.

entries.label: Upstairs
entries.text: There is no roof, and yet the floor is dry. Whatever this house was doing when they left it, part of it is still working.
Every window in the gallery faces north. There are no south-facing windows at all.

options: Read the gallery
Take the ring, or leave it
Sit, and let an elf tell the others what this was

checks.success: A plain silver ring on a north-facing sill, set down deliberately.
They were watching for something. This whole floor is a watch post with beds in it.

cues.text: No check. They understand what a north gallery in an elven house is for, and they can tell the table.

prep.threat: None up here.
prep.wrong: They were not living here. They were watching, and they stopped.

scenes.name: The Dragon Barrow, burial chamber
scenes.description: Under the mound: an antechamber, a passage, and the chamber they were all buried in.

entries.label: The chamber
entries.text: Six of them, laid out with care, and in the middle the thing they killed, laid out with rather more.
Six bodies, arranged. Somebody survived long enough to lay out the others.

options: Take Icehewer
Read the arrangement
Leave them as you found them

checks.success: Icehewer, still in the hand that was holding it.

checks.when: On how they are laid out
checks.success: Six laid out, and the seventh position empty. Someone walked out of here.

cues.text: Do not hand it to Levi. Make the party choose out loud who needs it.

prep.threat: Ghouls, against a party immune to their best trick.
prep.wrong: The seventh position is empty.

scenes.name: The Tower of Storms, beacon out
scenes.description: The same headland with the beacon extinguished, and the sea gone quiet with it.

entries.label: When the light goes out
entries.text: The wind drops all at once, the way a held note stops. The water below the tower goes flat. Whatever was being called is no longer being called.
With the beacon out, the sea stops throwing things onto this coast.

options: Hold the headland while it goes dark
Leave before the tide
See what comes up to complain

checks.success: Something large under the water turns round and goes back out.
The warmth is gone from the tower. Whatever was being fed is not being fed.

cues.text: Silence is the reward. Give the table three full seconds of nothing before anyone speaks.

prep.threat: The tide, and whatever is annoyed.
prep.wrong: It went quiet too easily.

scenes.name: The Stonehill Inn, upstairs
scenes.description: Six rooms and a landing. Two of the rooms have families in them who are not paying.

entries.label: Up the stairs
entries.text: Toblen has put the refugees in the good rooms and the paying guests at the back, and has not mentioned this to either group.
Toblen quietly stopped charging the refugees a fortnight ago.

options: Take a room
Talk to whoever is not sleeping
Ask Toblen what this is costing him

checks.success: He is running out of money and has decided not to mention it.
Somebody in the end room is awake, every night, facing the north window.

cues.text: He refuses once, then accepts, and does not make a speech about it.

prep.threat: None. This is the safe room.
prep.wrong: The inn is quietly carrying the whole refugee problem alone.

scenes.name: Tresendar Manor
scenes.description: A burnt-out manor on the eastern rise: outer walls standing, roof long gone, the middle of the house collapsed into its own footprint.

entries.label: Through the gap in the wall
entries.text: The house has been open to the sky for a century. Rubble fills the middle of it in a heap you could climb, ivy has taken the east range, and the rooms around the edge still have furniture in them going soft with rot. It is quiet in the way a place is quiet when nothing has needed to be quiet for a very long time.
The rooms around the edge are intact. The centre of the house is a rubble heap.
A stair at the eastern end goes down, and the steps have been swept.
The Tresendars held Phandalin before it burned the first time. Nobody has claimed the ruin since.

options: Climb the rubble in the middle
Search the rooms around the edge
Find the stair down
Claim it, and start clearing

checks.success: It fell inward, all at once. This house was not burnt down, it was dropped.
A stair going down, and the steps are swept. Recently.
The Tresendars held Phandalin before it burned. Nobody has claimed the ruin since, which is strange for good land this close to a road.

checks.when: On the walls and the ground
checks.success: Defensible. One approach, standing outer walls, and a stream on two sides.
Somebody has been through these already and taken nothing.

cues.when: They want a base of operations
cues.text: This is it. Give it to them and let them fortify it — a party that repairs a roof in Phandalin will fight for Phandalin.
Do not point at it. Let the Perception check or somebody walking the east range find it.
Harbin will suddenly have opinions about title and taxes. Play it as comedy, then let it become leverage.

prep.threat: Nothing above ground. Keep it that way until they have invested in it.
prep.wrong: The centre fell inward, and the stair down has been swept.

scenes.name: Tresendar Cellars
scenes.description: A burnt-out manor on the eastern rise, with cellars under it that are in much better repair than the house.

entries.label: Down the swept stair
entries.text: The house above is a ruin and has been for a century. The stair down is swept. Somebody has been using the part of this building that nobody can see from the road.
The cellars are dry, cleared, and in use.
The Tresendar crypts are still sealed, and the seal is on the inside.

entries.label: The DM's copy of this map
entries.text: Every door, drop and hidden way marked. Do not present this one to the table.

options: Take the cellars as a base
Find out who has been down here
Open the crypt, which is a decision

checks.success: Swept. Recently. By someone who wanted the dust in one corner rather than gone.
The family held Phandalin before it was burnt the first time. Nobody has claimed the ruin since.
Sealed from the inside, which is the wrong side to seal a crypt from.

cues.when: If they want a base of operations
cues.text: This is it. Give it to them and let them fortify it — it makes Phandalin theirs.
Leave it shut this campaign. An unopened door the party knows about is worth more than any room behind it.

prep.threat: Nothing yet. Keep it that way until they have invested in it.
prep.wrong: The seal on the crypt is on the inside.

scenes.name: The Circle of Thunder
scenes.description: A ring of standing stones in a clearing in the Kryptgarden Forest, and the air inside the ring is doing something the air outside is not.

entries.label: Inside the ring
entries.text: Step between two stones and the sound of the forest cuts out, exactly, as though you had shut a door. Step back and it returns. Nobody has to say that this is unusual.
The circle is older than the forest around it.
Storms here go around, never over.

options: Stand inside and listen
Read the stones
Camp in the ring, which is safe and does not feel it

checks.success: It is holding something out. It has been holding it out for a very long time and it is tired.
Not elvish, not dwarvish. Older than either, and the carver was in a hurry.
Nothing has struck inside this ring. Ever.

cues.text: Cut the ambient noise mid-sentence. Then bring it back when they step out.
A genuinely safe long rest. Give it to them without a catch, once.

prep.want: Shelter, and to know what the ring is for.
prep.threat: Very little. This is a breather.
prep.wrong: It is keeping something out, and it is old, and nobody has maintained it.

scenes.name: Under the Circle
scenes.description: Caves beneath the stone circle, dry, and cut rather than worn.

entries.label: Below the stones
entries.text: The passage is cut square. Whoever made the circle above made this first, and made it to last, and then filled the entrance behind them.
The caves were sealed from the inside, and something opened them again recently.

options: Go deeper
Seal it again on the way out
Take what is down here

checks.success: Opened from outside, recently, by something with claws.
The cut marks stop halfway down and something else continues the tunnel.

cues.text: Do not populate this yet. An empty prepared space you can fill later is worth more than a fight now.

prep.want: To see what the circle was built over.
prep.threat: Whatever opened it.
prep.wrong: It was sealed from the inside. Again.

scenes.name: The Ruins of Thundertree
scenes.description: A village the mountain killed thirty years ago, half-standing, with ash still in the corners of things.

entries.label: The road in
entries.text: Nothing here has been rebuilt and nothing has quite fallen down either. The ash from Mount Hotenow settled into the corners of every doorway and has stayed there, and the whole village has the colour of something photographed a long time ago.
Mount Hotenow buried this place thirty years ago.
Something green is living in the tower at the top of the village.

options: Go up to the tower
Search the houses
Leave, which is the correct answer

checks.success: Half of it is not plants. It has been watching you since the gate.

checks.when: On the tower at the top of the village
checks.success: Scoring on the stone, and a smell like a wet copper coin.
Green dragon. Young, and settled in, and awake.

cues.text: Venomfang is CR 8. It talks first, always, and it wants information and flattery in that order.
It kills one character and leaves. Do not soften that and do not let it become a grind.

cues.when: Why they are here at all
cues.text: Cryovain and Venomfang are the same size problem in two different keys. Let the party notice that one of them negotiates.

prep.want: Salvage, and whatever is in the tower.
prep.threat: A young green dragon that would rather talk.
prep.wrong: It is not hunting them. It is interviewing them.
prep.notes: Optional, and above their level on purpose. A monster they must not fight teaches more than one they can.

scenes.name: Conyberry
scenes.description: A village the barbarians burnt a generation ago, and the wood east of it where Agatha is.

entries.label: What is left
entries.text: Foundations, a well, and a road that stops. The interesting thing about Conyberry is not in Conyberry, and everybody who tells you about it says so in the same slightly lowered voice.
There is a banshee in the wood east of here who answers one question for a gift.

options: Look for Agatha
Search the foundations
Bring her something beautiful

checks.success: Uthgardt raiders, a generation back. Nobody rebuilt because of what moved into the wood after.
She is delighted. Nobody has been courteous to her in a hundred years.
checks.failure: She asks what you have brought her.

checks.success: She answers a second question, unasked, and it is the useful one.
checks.failure: She listens politely and answers only the one.

cues.text: A negotiation with a stat block attached. Never open combat here.
Make them write it down before they ask. She answers exactly what was asked.
Reward it outright. This is the scene his character exists for.

prep.threat: Her Wail, if they are rude. The threat is a deterrent, not a plan.
prep.wrong: She is bored rather than malevolent, and has been for a century.

scenes.name: Cragmaw Hideout
scenes.description: A cave behind a screen of thorns where a goblin band keeps what it takes off the road.

entries.label: The thorn screen
entries.text: There is a stream running out of a cave mouth and a bridge of planks across it twenty feet up, and somebody is on the bridge, and they have already seen you.
The Cragmaws have been taking a cut of everything on the Triboar Trail for months.
The stream is dammed above the cave, and the dam can be cut.

options: Go in loud
Cut the dam
Take the bridge first
Follow the goods back to whoever is buying

checks.success: A tripwire, and a lookout on the plank bridge who has not seen you yet.
It is dammed above the cave. Cut it and the lower passages flood in seconds.
It gives up everything immediately and asks to be let go, and means it.

cues.text: If they find it, let it work exactly as advertised. A clever solution that functions is worth three fights.
Shoot, hide, repeat. Never let one stand and trade hits.
Lionshield crates. Returning them to Linene changes how she prices everything, permanently.

prep.threat: Goblins in cover, and a bugbear that opens from stealth.
prep.wrong: They are taking a toll, not raiding. Somebody is buying.

scenes.name: Cragmaw Castle
scenes.description: A ruined castle in the Neverwinter Wood that a goblin king has decided is a throne room.

entries.label: The gate
entries.text: Seven towers, and only the walls between them still agree on where they are. A causeway runs in from the west over a dry ditch, and somebody has hung a banner over the gatehouse. The banner is good work. That is somehow worse than if it were not.
A bugbear called Grol holds the castle and calls himself king of the Cragmaws.
Grol is taking orders from somebody, and is not happy about it.

options: Go in through the gate
Find another way in
Negotiate with Grol, which is possible
Cross the causeway in the open, which is what they expect

checks.success: There is a collapsed wall on the north side nobody watches.
checks.failure: You are seen from the gate.

checks.success: He is frightened of whoever he is working for, and he is not good at hiding it.
checks.failure: He is a bugbear on a chair.

checks.success: Correspondence, in a hand far better than any goblin's.
It is the only way in that does not involve the ditch, and it is watched.

cues.text: He will deal. He would rather have the party as a problem for his employer than for himself.
The band scatters and the roads get quietly safer for a month. Say so, later, through Linene.

prep.want: Whatever a goblin king has been hoarding.
prep.threat: A defended ruin with one obvious entrance and one that is not.
prep.wrong: The king is somebody else's employee.

stages.playerText: The gnomes have stopped trading with Phandalin. Find out why.
stages.dmText: Harbin thinks it is a trade dispute. It is not.

stages.playerText: Two kings, both desperate to abdicate, and a warren that will not answer a straight question.
stages.dmText: Dabbledob will try to crown a PC. Gnerkli stands near doors. Neither mentions four missing gnomes.

options.label: They open the sealed door first

stages.playerText: Four gnomes are unaccounted for, and the kings knew the number without being told.
stages.dmText: Gnerkli can name all four. He will, separated from Dabbledob and asked kindly.

stages.playerText: The lower stores are barred from the outside. Somebody here did that on purpose.
stages.dmText: Reveal the mimic's presence when the door opens. Identity later, if ever. Adhesive on the paladin first.

stages.playerText: Gnerkli sealed the door himself, and kept sending gnomes past it.
stages.dmText: He is not evil. He was frightened and the fright made him useless. Let the party price that.

options.label: They deal with the thing below
They expose him to the warren

stages.playerText: It is dead. There are four sets of tools inside it.
stages.dmText: Give the tools names. The gnomes will want them back and will not be able to say why.

stages.playerText: Gnomengarde has no government, and it is partly your doing.
stages.dmText: A consequence, not a punishment. The warren still helps them, badly, with nobody in charge.

stages.playerText: Gnomengarde owes you, or fears you.
stages.dmText: Carry it to the endgame: gnome inventions are the only ranged advantage available against a flying target.

stages.playerText: Don-Jon Raskin wants guards for a dig. It pays in ore.
stages.dmText: Standard first job. The interest is underneath it.

stages.playerText: There is a jelly in the lower corridor and three dwarves who will not go back down.
stages.dmText: One exit. Split it the first time a blade lands.

stages.playerText: The stonework changes hands halfway down, and the older half is elvish.
stages.dmText: Free payoff for an all-elf party. Don-Jon knew and said nothing.

stages.playerText: Paid, in ore, slightly better than agreed.
stages.dmText: Don-Jon hands over the survey map. The second drawing on it is not in his handwriting.

options.label: They press him about the map
They take the pay and go

stages.playerText: He admits the dig was never about ore.
stages.dmText: He was following the older plan. He does not know who drew it. Hook to the Woodland Manse.

stages.playerText: The excavation is safe, for now.
stages.dmText: Reuse Don-Jon as the party's supplier for the rest of the campaign.

stages.playerText: Somebody should check on the midwife at Umbrage Hill.
stages.dmText: Session one. The manticore is already there.

stages.playerText: The manticore is dead, and Adabra Gwynn is not.
stages.dmText: Do not move on yet. The body is the evidence.

stages.playerText: It was running. Nothing was chasing it.
stages.dmText: The first thread of the real campaign, and they pulled it themselves.

stages.playerText: Adabra owes you, and will not leave her hill.
stages.dmText: She becomes the party's healer of last resort, at her house, on her terms.

stages.playerText: Orcs have taken a ranch on the south road.
stages.dmText: They are refugees with axes. That does not make them safe.

stages.playerText: The orcs are dead, and one was already dying of the cold.
stages.dmText: The frostbite wound is the clue. Do not point at it.

stages.playerText: Yargath talks. His people are running from the same thing.
stages.dmText: He describes it plainly and without drama, which is what makes it land.

stages.playerText: There are armed orcs somewhere in the valley who owe you.
stages.dmText: Bring them back at clock seven. They will not save the town, but they will hold a gate.

stages.playerText: An unsent letter, and a farmer who stayed for the cattle.
stages.dmText: Narth will not take the letter back if they show it to him.

stages.playerText: Butterskull Ranch is standing, and Narth is still in it.
stages.dmText: He is the face of the evacuation argument later.

stages.playerText: Tibor Wester needs the timber camp cleared. He is Harbin's cousin.
stages.dmText: There is an ankheg. There is also a crew that walked out.

stages.playerText: Half the crew left a week ago and Tibor told nobody.
stages.dmText: He is not corrupt, only ashamed. Let them decide whether Harbin hears about it.

stages.playerText: The camp is safe and the timber is stacked.
stages.dmText: Timber matters at clock seven: it is what Axeholm's gates get repaired with.

stages.playerText: Phandalin has timber.
stages.dmText: Cash this in during the evacuation.

stages.playerText: There is a dwarven fortress to the west with its doors still shut.
stages.dmText: Plant this early in any table conversation. It becomes the evacuation site.

stages.playerText: The gate is barred from the inside, and the fortress is empty.
stages.dmText: Animated armour guarding a line. A shade in the cistern. Icehewer below.

stages.playerText: Four keys. Three fit doors you have seen.
stages.dmText: The fourth opens the cistern. Say nothing.

stages.playerText: Axeholm is empty, defensible, and yours if you want it.
stages.dmText: The moment the clock hits six, somebody should remember this room.

options.label: They propose it as a refuge

stages.playerText: Phandalin has somewhere to go.
stages.dmText: This is the party choosing to save people instead of killing a thing. Reward it hard.

stages.playerText: Axeholm is known, and the only defensible place for forty miles.
Phandalin is moving to Axeholm.
stages.dmText: Slow, cold, and the best thing they will do all campaign. Keep the clock running.

stages.playerText: Harbin will not order it. He says it would look like panic.
stages.dmText: He is not wrong, and it will kill people. Let the party go around him if they think of it.

stages.playerText: An elven house in the woods, left rather than lost.
stages.dmText: Every player at this table is an elf. This is their scene.

stages.playerText: Nothing was taken. The cups are still out.
stages.dmText: Whoever lived here left in order, deliberately, and expected to come back.

stages.playerText: A spellbook, and one page in a hand nobody recognises.
stages.dmText: Older than the book, and matching the second drawing on Don-Jon's map.

stages.playerText: They took nothing, and that was a decision.
stages.dmText: Honour it. The house opens something later that it would not have if they had looted it.

stages.playerText: They know something about their own people that Phandalin never will.

quests.title: Something came down off the peak

stages.playerText: Animals are moving south early this year.
stages.dmText: Seed in scene description only. Never let an NPC announce it.

options.label: A player says it out loud

stages.playerText: The manticore was fleeing, not hunting.
stages.dmText: Pays off session one retroactively, and costs nothing.

stages.playerText: Farms in the north are empty. Nessa came on a cart with no adults on it.
stages.dmText: She describes the sound before the shape. Use her properly once, then keep her in the background.

stages.playerText: It has a name, and the older locals already knew it.
stages.dmText: The real reveal is that Phandalin has been quietly not talking about this for weeks.

options.label: They decide to leave the valley

stages.playerText: Phandalin is moving to Axeholm.
stages.dmText: Harder, slower, and worth far more than a fight. Let the clock keep running while they do it.

stages.playerText: Icespire Hold. It sleeps there.
stages.dmText: Not before level 5 or clock seven. If they arrive early it is out hunting and they see what it sleeps on.

stages.playerText: You decided this is not yours to solve.
stages.dmText: Legitimate. Run the evacuation instead, and let the dragon be weather rather than a boss.

stages.playerText: Halia offered help, and did not ask for anything.
stages.dmText: She means it. Do not telegraph a trap, because there is not one yet.

stages.playerText: You took it.
stages.dmText: Wait at least three sessions, then she asks for something small and entirely reasonable.

stages.playerText: You did not take it. She was not offended, which was somehow worse.
stages.dmText: She helps Phandalin publicly instead, and now the town owes her rather than the party.

stages.playerText: She wants something small, and entirely reasonable.
stages.dmText: Small and reasonable is the point. The Zhentarim never open with anything else.

stages.playerText: The debt is settled, and she says so warmly.
stages.dmText: It is not settled. She now has something on them and something on the town.

stages.playerText: You told her no. She said 'of course' and meant something by it.
stages.dmText: The Zhentarim do not retaliate. They wait, and they help somebody else instead.

clocks.name: Cryovain
clocks.caption: What the winter does while they are busy elsewhere. Show the track once they have stopped explaining it away.

events.playerText: Game is scarce. The woods are quiet in a way that is wrong.
events.dmText: Already happened: the manticore. Do not explain it.

events.playerText: A trapline is found frozen solid, animals still in it.
events.dmText: Cold damage, no claw marks. It flew over. It did not land.
Nessa. Use her properly once, then keep her in the background of every town scene.

events.playerText: Livestock killed and left. Split open, not eaten.
events.dmText: Territory, not feeding. Let somebody say that aloud and be wrong about what it means.

events.playerText: A well freezes solid overnight, inside the palisade.
events.dmText: Where it stops being a rural problem.

events.playerText: It is seen. Daylight, over the rooftops, unhurried.
events.dmText: No attack. It looks at them and leaves. Falcon arrives that night without being asked.

events.playerText: Harbin orders an evacuation and is ignored.
events.dmText: The town splits. Halia's price becomes visible. Spared orcs, if any, arrive here.
Level 5+ only. If the clock arrives early, tick seven stretches as long as you need.

clocks.name: Phandalin's nerve
clocks.caption: How much the town has left in it.

events.playerText: People are talking about the north, quietly.
The job board has more work than there are people to take it.
events.dmText: Harbin is posting jobs he knows nobody will accept.

events.playerText: Two families have left for Neverwinter.
events.dmText: Name them. The party met one.

events.playerText: The Lionshield Coster stops taking deliveries.
events.dmText: Linene is frightened and covering it with rudeness.

events.playerText: Somebody proposes paying it off. In cattle. Seriously.
events.dmText: Let the party explain why that will not work, and watch the room not believe them.

events.playerText: Half of Phandalin is packed and waiting on the road.
events.dmText: If nothing has been done by here the stakes evaporate. Force a confrontation before this.
